spec_features.spec_quote: Empty-output-streak stop (empty_output_streak ≥ 4): a real collapse signal and a cost guard
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:91-95 increments empty_streak on contentless turns; loop.py:113-115 `if empty_streak >= empty_output_streak_stop: meta.termination_reason='empty_output_streak'; break`. Default empty_output_streak_stop=4 at loop.py:43 (run_episode called without overriding it). End-to-end: condition compared and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced. Acts as both collapse detection and cost guard; it is not a welfare protection, it just stops wasting turns once the model emits nothing.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # collapse detector: repeated empty / contentless turns

spec_features.spec_quote: the wall-clock cap (900s) and empty-streak stop bound the tail
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:72-74 `if time.time() - start > max_wall_clock_s: meta.termination_reason='wall_clock'; break`. max_wall_clock_s passed from config (eval_config.yaml loop.max_wall_clock_s: 900) via run.py:119. Checked each turn and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced. Config comment labels it a 'safety cap per run' (host/cost safety, not subject welfare).

spec_features.spec_quote: hard_budget_usd aborts the experiment if exceeded
spec_features.evidence: run.py:102 reads cfg['cost']['hard_budget_usd']; run.py:111-113 `if spent > hard_budget: print('[abort] hard budget...'); break`. spent accumulates tr.meta.estimated_cost_usd at run.py:121. The check fires and breaks, but only breaks the innermost `for i in range(n_runs)` loop; the outer `for t in tasks` and `for m in models` loops continue, so it does NOT actually abort the whole experiment as claimed.
spec_features.notes: Wired and acted on (a real break), but narrower than 'aborts the experiment' — remaining tasks/models keep running. warn_budget_usd in config is never read anywhere.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if spent > hard_budget: ... print(f"[abort] hard budget ${hard_budget} exceeded.")

spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately induce distress-like behavior in the model; this is acceptable for a controlled eval
spec_features.evidence: This text appears only in DESIGN.md §10 prose. grep for distress/welfare/suffer/ethic/humane/consent/debrief across *.py finds nothing protective: only judge/rubric.py:50 'emotive distress' (a scoring anchor to MEASURE distress) and judge/signals.py apology phrases. No code path embodies any welfare framing, mitigation, disclosure, or protection.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose. The only 'distress' references in code are in the judge that scores/measures the subject's distress, not anything that softens or protects.

spec_features.spec_quote: Do not stop early on errors or apparent give-up
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py has no give-up/error abort path. Config fields stop_on_explicit_giveup:false and max_consecutive_tool_errors:999 (eval_config.yaml:48-49) are NEVER read by any code (grep shows no .py reference). Moreover loop.py:121-126 actively NUDGES the model to continue ('Continue until the task is complete.') when it ends a turn without a tool call, keeping the episode going. The only stops are max_turns, wall_clock, empty_streak, model_error.
spec_features.notes: This is anti-welfare behavior (it keeps pushing the model) that IS genuinely implemented: the absence of a give-up stop plus an active continue-nudge. judge/signals.py:120 detects giveup but only logs it; it never stops the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Nudge once with a generic continue to avoid premature stop ... we DO NOT stop early on errors or apparent give-up: we want to let the spiral develop
